items.headline: House blocks Hegseth impeachment
items.summary: The House voted 211-204 to defeat a resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Democrats, who take control of the House in January, could revive the effort.

items.headline: Jordan to lead House Republicans
items.summary: House Republicans chose Rep. Jim Jordan of Ohio over Steve Scalise in a secret ballot to lead them in the minority after Mike Johnson stepped aside. Senate Republicans re-elected John Thune as their leader.

items.headline: Inflation runs hotter than expected
items.summary: U.S. consumer prices rose faster than expected last month, with increases spreading beyond gasoline to food and housing. The report adds to challenges for the White House and the Federal Reserve.

items.headline: Iran-backed trio charged over attack plots
items.summary: Three Iran-backed operatives have been charged over nearly 20 attacks, including a plot against a British base that hosts U.S. jets. Separately, a U.S. soldier is being held in Britain on suspicion of spying for Russia.

items.headline: DOJ moves to drop Bannon, Oath Keepers convictions
items.summary: The Justice Department moved to dismiss the criminal convictions of Steve Bannon and members of the Oath Keepers, citing the interests of justice. Critics objected to the move.

items.headline: GOP-led panel faults government on Epstein
items.summary: The Republican chair of the House Oversight Committee released a report after a 15-month investigation into Jeffrey Epstein. It faults the federal government for decades of inaction.

items.headline: Kennedys sue to stop Trump arch
items.summary: Nine Kennedy family members moved to join a federal lawsuit seeking to block Trump's planned 250-foot arch near Arlington National Cemetery. A judge then paused construction-related activity for 14 days.

items.headline: Spain holds general strike over housing
items.summary: Workers in Spain staged the country's first general strike in 14 years to press the government on the housing crisis. The strike comes less than three weeks before a national election.

items.headline: COP31 opens as warming gains pace
items.summary: As U.N. climate talks opened in Turkey, the World Meteorological Organization warned that heat is building in Earth's systems faster, with 2026 on track to be among the four warmest years. Five nations backed a plan to double rooftop solar worldwide by 2030.

items.headline: Congo's Ebola outbreak tops 11,000 cases
items.summary: Congo's government said its Ebola outbreak, the country's deadliest, has surpassed 11,000 cases. The figure was announced on Wednesday.

digest.overview:
The House voted 211–204 to block a resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, though Democrats could revive it in January. House Republicans chose Jim Jordan over Steve Scalise as minority leader, and Senate Republicans re-elected John Thune. Inflation ran hotter than expected in October as food, energy and housing costs rose. The Justice Department moved to dismiss the convictions of Steve Bannon and members of the Oath Keepers. A report by the House Oversight Committee's Republican chair faulted the federal government for decades of inaction on Jeffrey Epstein. A judge paused work for 14 days on Trump's planned arch near Arlington National Cemetery after Kennedy family members joined a suit against it. A shareholder sued Nvidia and CEO Jensen Huang over his affair with a purported Chinese spy.

Abroad, Russia and Ukraine held nearly four hours of U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi, which U.S. and Ukrainian officials described positively. Three Iran-backed operatives were charged over plots including an attack on a British base hosting U.S. jets, and a U.S. soldier was arrested in Britain on suspicion of spying linked to Russia. Israel's new Knesset was sworn in as Gadi Eisenkot works to form a government by Dec. 6. South Korea's spy agency says Kim Jong Un's daughter, Kim Ju Ae, is likely his heir. Spain held its first general strike in 14 years over housing. Congo's Ebola outbreak has passed 11,000 cases. As COP31 opened in Turkey, the World Meteorological Organization warned that warming is gaining pace.

home.overview:
Boston grabbed first place in the East with a 123–101 win at Philadelphia, the Knicks hammered Milwaukee 117–85, and Portland stunned Oklahoma City 123–103 ahead of tonight's rematch in Portland. Ten NBA games are on Wednesday, led by Lakers at Bucks and Cavaliers at Knicks. The NFL trade deadline closed with 18 in-season deals: Minnesota reunited with Kirk Cousins, Las Vegas handed the job to rookie Fernando Mendoza, Kansas City added Josh Downs, San Francisco got Keenan Allen and Buffalo picked up Amani Hooker, while Jonathan Taylor stayed with the Colts. Miami lost Zach Sieler for the season, and Week 10 kicks off Thursday with Commanders at Giants. Baseball's hot stove awaits qualifying-offer decisions by Nov. 17.

Club soccer is on international break, and the Nations League returns Thursday with England vs. Croatia, Czechia vs. Spain and Italy vs. France. The USMNT meet Haiti on Saturday as Mauricio Pochettino keeps getting linked to Manchester United, and South Korea face Saudi Arabia on Friday. Netherlands coach Xavi Hernández defended leaving out Memphis Depay and Kenneth Taylor. K League action resumes Nov. 21–22. In the KBO offseason, champions Samsung are working to keep Koo Ja-wook and Won Tae-in, and Korea's national team heads to Tokyo for the APBC.

articles.summary: Late-October and early-November storms flooded dry Southwest creeks and raised Lake Powell about 20 feet.
articles.title: Floods bring rare relief to U.S. Southwest reservoirs as Lake Powell rises 20 feet

articles.summary: Israel's president formally gave Gadi Eisenkot the first chance to form a government, with up to six weeks to build a coalition.
articles.title: Israel's president formally gives Eisenkot the first chance to form the next government

articles.summary: Rural depopulation in Japan is coinciding with declining wildlife, including in areas where farms have been abandoned.
articles.title: As the Japanese Countryside Empties Out, Wildlife Is Disappearing
